summary: The Aalto University Excellence Scholarship is a tuition fee waiver given by Aalto to a very limited number of top applicants who must pay tuition fees, for English-taught bachelor's and master's programmes in Espoo, Finland. It is merit-based and is requested inside the admission application. It pays the tuition fee only; living and study costs stay with the student.
eligibility_notes:
Only applicants who are liable for tuition fees can apply. In general that means citizens of countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland, for English-taught bachelor's and master's programmes. EU, EEA and Swiss citizens do not pay tuition fees and cannot apply. People with certain Finnish residence permits valid on 1 August of the start year are exempt from fees (for example permanent residence, EU long-term residence, EU Blue Card, a family member card of an EU citizen held personally, Brexit withdrawal-agreement permits, and temporary protection permits). A continuous (type A) permit can exempt a person if it was granted on a ground other than study; the exemption is lost if the first Finnish permit was for study or a family permit traces back to a study permit. Holders of such permits must upload the permit card, both sides.

The scholarship must be requested in the admission application form by answering yes to the scholarship question during the application period; it cannot be requested later. Applying does not affect admission chances. Candidates admitted from the waiting list cannot receive a scholarship. Scholarship candidates are checked against EU sanctions lists.

A master's applicant must hold a bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS or three years of full-time study that gives master's eligibility in the awarding country, from a recognised institution, and must prove language proficiency. A previous master's degree does not qualify, apart from long-cycle degrees. A bachelor's degree may be incomplete at application if it is awarded by 31 July 2027. Art and design applicants without a degree may apply on the basis of equivalent skills and experience. Business and economics applicants with foreign degrees (Admission Group 2) must submit GMAT or GRE scores. English-taught bachelor's applicants must hold an upper-secondary qualification that qualifies for higher education.

The award is tied to the study option it was granted for; a scholarship for a lower-ranked option does not move to a first-choice option, and it is lost if that place is not accepted. Scholarships are not reallocated. Studies must be full-time and follow an approved personal study plan.
age_experience_notes: No age limit and no work experience requirement stated on the pages read.
funding_summary: The scholarship waives the tuition fee for the normative length of the programme: 3 years for a bachelor's degree and 2 years for a master's degree. It does not cover living costs or other study-related costs. It continues during exchange or internships abroad, but the tuition fee must still be paid during that time. The pages say students need at least EUR 800 per month for living costs, and that the capital region is more expensive.
programmes_note: Eleven English-taught bachelor's programmes (Design and Media; Economics; Finance; International Business; Chemical Engineering; Mechanical and Civil Engineering; Computer Engineering; Data Science; Digital Systems and Design; Quantum Technology; Technology, Business and Design) and about 75 master's study options in art, design and architecture; business and economics; and technology and engineering. Some master's options are international joint degrees with their own funding and application rules. Programmes may decide not to award any scholarships; each programme's evaluation criteria are on its own page.
institutions_note: Aalto University, Espoo, Finland (art and design, business, and technology schools). Applicants choose study options when applying: up to two in the master's admission and up to three in an English-taught bachelor's round.

summary.detail: The scholarship is given for the 3-year normative bachelor's period. Annual tuition fees for rights to study starting on or after 1 August 2025 are EUR 12,000 (Business), EUR 15,000 (Art and Architecture), EUR 12,000 (Technology) and EUR 12,000 (the multidisciplinary Technology, Business and Design programme). Applications for autumn 2027 run from 7 to 22 January 2027 in round A (SAT or ACT based) or round B (grades based; Design and Media on assignments and interview); the fee is EUR 100 for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens. Bachelor graduates who held the scholarship and finish in target time with a weighted average of at least 3.5 can get a 100 percent waiver for a direct-right Aalto master's.

summary.detail: The scholarship is given for the 2-year normative master's period and decided during the academic evaluation of admissions, with the admission decision. Annual tuition fees are EUR 15,000 (Business), EUR 20,000 (Art and Architecture), EUR 17,000 (Technology) and EUR 17,000 for the multidisciplinary options (Creative Sustainability; International Design Business Management; Urban Studies and Planning). Applicants may choose up to two study options, ranked. The programme list pages do not state the teaching language of each option, and a few options are taught in Finnish or Swedish.

application_steps.title: Choose study options and check fee status
application_steps.detail: Read the eligibility rules, study option criteria and document instructions. Master's applicants rank up to two options; English-taught bachelor's applicants rank up to three in one round (round A or round B). Only fee-liable applicants can ask for the Excellence Scholarship.

application_steps.title: Submit the application form and answer yes to the scholarship question
application_steps.detail: The master's application form opens 7 December 2026 at 09:00 and closes 5 January 2027 at 23:59 (UTC+2). English-taught bachelor's applications run 7 to 22 January 2027. Only one form is allowed, edits are possible until the period ends, and the scholarship question must be answered inside this period.

application_steps.title: Pay the application fee and upload documents
application_steps.detail: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens pay EUR 100 through the national admissions service within seven days of submitting. Master's documents, language proof and test scores must be uploaded by 12 January 2027 at 23:59 (UTC+2); the deadlines are strict and incomplete applications are not evaluated.

application_steps.title: Evaluation by each study option
application_steps.detail: Complete, eligible applications are ranked by each option's own criteria such as relevance of previous study, academic performance, motivation, portfolios, interviews or assignments. The Excellence Scholarship goes to the top-ranked fee-liable applicants during the academic evaluation; programmes may award none. Admission and scholarship decisions are issued together, no updates are given during evaluation, and scholarship decisions cannot be appealed. Bachelor's selection uses SAT or ACT (round A) or grades (round B), with assignments for some programmes.

application_steps.title: Results and acceptance
application_steps.detail: Master's results come on 30 March 2027 at the earliest by email; the offer must be accepted, binding, by 21 April 2027 at 23:59 (UTC+3). Waiting-list admissions end 14 June 2027, and a person admitted from the waiting list cannot receive a scholarship. Bachelor's results are by 31 March 2027 (round A) or 28 May 2027 (round B). A written rectification request for procedural errors can be sent within 14 days of publication.

application_steps.title: Certified documents and enrolment
application_steps.detail: Admitted master's students send officially certified copies by the deadline set for their admission date (13 May 2027 for those admitted 30 March to 4 April, 17 August 2027 for later admissions); admission stays conditional until they arrive. Students pay their own costs and cannot enrol until any fee that applies is paid; new students are advised to pay by 31 July. Residence permit or fee exemption must be valid on 1 August 2027.

application_steps.title: Keep the waiver by studying full-time
application_steps.detail: The waiver lasts for the normative period and depends on full-time study and progress under the approved study plan. Bachelor's scholarship holders who graduate within three years with a weighted average of at least 3.5 can receive a 100 percent waiver for the 2-year master's in programmes with a direct right to continue.
